newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand PM promises "damn good budget".
newsitem.headline: New Zealand PM promises "damn good budget".

text.p: New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Wednesday next week's Budget would be "a damned good Budget" building on recent moves such as the deregulation of the New Zealand postal service.

"It will build on such moves as postal deregulation and developments in education and land transport administration. It will indicate the government is continuing with a forward- looking policy," Bolger told parliament.
The document will be the National/New Zealand First coalition's debut budget.
"It will draw together the themes of growth and development in economic and social policy and spell out clear priorities to take New Zealand into the next century," the Premier said.

"These priorities will emphasise our commitment to a strong outward-looking economy and building up the social capital as well as the economic capital of New Zealand. In other words it will be a damned good Budget," he added.
The government has promised NZ$950 million in new spending initiatives in the Budget.
It has said it will maintain surpluses, although slower- than-expected growth would mean they were lower than the track it forecast in a March policy statement.
That projection forecast a surplus of $3.2 billion in 1997/98 and $2.6 billion in 1998/99.
The Budget will be tabled in parliament at 2 p.m. (0200 GMT) on June 26.
